allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 10 m at 30 years and 20 m at 60. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: glaucous grey-green fronds, brown leaf bases.

generator.params.note: Wikipedia, Date palm (read 2026-10-14): up to 30 m, single or in a clump of stems from one root system; leaves 4 to 6 m long (frond_length 4.8), spined on the petiole, pinnate with about 150 leaflets (38 pieces of rachis, about 76 a side), the leaflets 30 cm long and 2 cm wide (leaflet_length 0.07 of the frond, cards of aspect 0.07); a crown 6 to 10 m across. Set by eye from general knowledge of the species: a rough trunk clothed in old leaf bases, stiff grey-green fronds whose leaflets stand in a V and 15 degrees above and below it, the oldest hanging 20 degrees lower over their life, and offshoots at the base. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.dead_angle.note: Dransfield et al. (Genera Palmarum, 2nd ed., 2008), under the genus: its dead leaves stay on the stem (marcescent) rather than falling cleanly.

generator.params.dead_life.note: Dransfield et al. (Genera Palmarum, 2nd ed., 2008), under the genus: its dead leaves stay on the stem (marcescent) rather than falling cleanly.

generator.params.fan_arch.note: What the palm program's values mean for a palm's stated characters: its frond is its whole leaf; fan or feather from its division pattern, with the petiole, its girth, rachis pieces and frond angles of the built-in fan or feather palms; suckers if it is clonal; the trunk's rise from its usual height less the crown, and its girth from its stated diameter or else its height.

generator.params.skirt.note: Dransfield et al. (Genera Palmarum, 2nd ed., 2008), under the genus: its dead leaves stay on the stem (marcescent) rather than falling cleanly.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the palm base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the palm program gave as defaults until then.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy (plant forms milestone F4). Calibration against measurements and photographs comes later.
